Release 1 decision: All MOSAIC orchestrator implementation remains with the MOSAIC owner.
Rationale: Developers work through published contracts and explicit dependency gates.
Replacement or follow-on: This boundary applies to Release 1 and future orchestrator changes.

Release 1 decision: Goals, planning, routing, capability execution, Goal-time Skill resolution and orchestration state are not delegated.
Rationale: These areas define MOSAIC behaviour and require coherent ownership.
Replacement or follow-on: Non-orchestrator teams may propose contracts and acceptance criteria but do not implement the runtime changes.

Release 1 decision: Release 1 is a controlled, invite-only development pilot.
Rationale: It demonstrates the complete user value path without claiming production readiness.
Replacement or follow-on: Production controls follow after real usage.

Release 1 decision: Reuse the existing orchestrator, Git catalogue and JSON snapshot.
Rationale: Replacing working mechanisms would add schedule risk without improving the pilot outcome.
Replacement or follow-on: Each temporary mechanism has a named follow-on epic.

Release 1 decision: Use Human Accounts with revocable development bearer tokens.
Rationale: This establishes trusted Account ownership with much less work than OIDC.
Replacement or follow-on: OIDC and independent Service identities are F1.

Release 1 decision: Every Session and enabled-Skill set belongs to one Account.
Rationale: The pilot proves isolation with two Accounts while retaining the intended multi-user boundary.
Replacement or follow-on: No shared workspace or team entity is introduced.

Release 1 decision: ADA persists conversation and runtime Session state; the access API persists ownership mappings.
Rationale: MOSAIC does not duplicate ADA Session storage.
Replacement or follow-on: Retention and administration follow observed usage.

Release 1 decision: Allow one active request per Session and concurrent work across different Sessions.
Rationale: This avoids queueing and conflicting state mutations.
Replacement or follow-on: Production limits are added later with exact 429 behaviour.

Release 1 decision: Use the current Goal and clarification behaviour in Release 1; ORCH-1 is the only planned runtime change.
Rationale: New cancellation and topic-switching semantics remain owner-controlled orchestrator work.

Release 1 decision: All Public Skills are visible; Accounts enable individual Skills or an explicit current group.
Rationale: Users need discovery and personal selection to experience the product value.
Replacement or follow-on: Private, restricted and marketplace authoring are F4.

Release 1 decision: Load the current validated JSON from a pinned reviewed Git revision.
Rationale: This gives every stateless replica the same startup configuration with minimal change.
Replacement or follow-on: Normalized PostgreSQL Integration publication is F3.

Release 1 decision: Use development data and read-only MCP servers with shared provider access.
Rationale: This is acceptable only for the development pilot and avoids premature shim work.
Replacement or follow-on: Delegated provider identity and RBAC are F2.

Release 1 decision: Use REST commands and SSE streaming.
Rationale: These match the current interaction and avoid unnecessary realtime infrastructure.
Replacement or follow-on: WebSockets are considered only if later features require them.

Release 1 decision: Provision Accounts and tokens through controlled CLI or SQL tooling.
Rationale: An administration UI is not necessary for a small invited pilot.

Release 1 decision: Rely on ADA/GCP logging and telemetry for the pilot.
Rationale: Duplicating telemetry before confirming gaps creates avoidable work.
Replacement or follow-on: Usage attribution and chargeback are F7.
